sourceLocation: Installed package inspected by user-approved Cursor extraction; SHA256 pins exact local source bytes
protocolChanges: Wire formats and existing callable/export surfaces retained. Initial extraction removed types/compiled enums and changed module paths; later refactoring separates modules, shares formatting/checkpoint logic and uses table-driven protocol dispatch.

files.transform: jiti enum-capable TypeScript compile to CommonJS

adaptations.vendorLint: Four scoped anti-slop spacing/naming/type style exemptions; ordinary correctness and syntax rules remain enabled

sourceSemanticVerification.appliesTo: Initial extraction only; not a whole-file AST identity claim for subsequent refactoring.

refactoring.generatedProto: Complete exports retained; redundant generated declarations/erased-type padding and unused local aliases removed; exact exported descriptor/enum initializer execution retained and schema/wire parity verified against the local baseline.
refactoring.runtime: Named acyclic module boundaries, role/exec/query dispatch, unified confirmation/catalog/usage helpers and shared completion/checkpoint operations.
refactoring.verification: Package suite plus old/new behavioral and byte-level comparisons. No upstream endpoint, entitlement or remote prompt-cache certification.

runtimeCorrections: Credential-scoped discovered catalogs and effort fallback; refreshed provider registrations retain their discovery callbacks.
Paused tool Runs resume only for the same credential/model and streaming format; changed scope rebuilds history under a new conversation generation.
Bridge completion follows child close/stdout drainage, including spawn failures; upstream failure is an error, not successful partial output.
Streaming and nonstreaming failure/cancellation terminate bridge children; nonstream responses use transport and useful-output watchdogs.
Intentional termination after turnEnded preserves successful checkpoints.
Cancellation/terminal failure advances conversation generation and invalidates partial checkpoints; paused SSE completion is not successful Run completion.
Checkpoint/blob commits are fenced to their captured conversation; late collectors and bridge cleanup cannot modify replacement Runs. Settled JSON ignores intentional-cancel terminal frames.
Runtime shutdown terminates all spawned bridge children, aborts owned OAuth workflows, and closes the proxy listener and HTTP connections; session transitions still use per-session cleanup.
Proxy startup is shared, cancellation/bind failures reject, and ensureCursorProxy rebinds after a stopped runtime rather than returning a dead cached port.

Unary deadlines settle without waiting for process close; AbortSignal propagates through login polling, refresh, and optional catalog RPC. OAuth HTTP requests/body reads are bounded to 15 seconds by default.

Transcript ownership includes canonical instructions/tools/completed-prefix identity and Pi-visible current-turn steps; only unchanged pending calls may receive new results. Edited/rewound history or abandoned pauses rebuild rather than resuming stale checkpoints.
Each fresh Run has a distinct collector owner while valid paused continuations retain their owner; overlapping collectors cannot overwrite newer checkpoint/blob state.

Cursor restoration preflights all requested provider IDs and rechecks foreign ownership at registration after async setup; only successful definitions enter the registered ownership set, permitting safe partial-setup retry.
Rebuilt current turns retain an immutable Pi-visible replay prefix separately from native Run steps; only results for current native pending calls may extend a pause.

Cursor ownership reconciles current SDK shallow-merged legacy definitions rather than treating previously registered IDs as perpetual ownership; late catalogs recheck current permission and released IDs can be primed again. Saved explicit transport/auth config protects offline bootstrap before the registry exists.
Coalesced native tool batches recheck conversation ownership at delivery; replaced/forgotten Runs fail without emitting queued tools or disturbing replacement state.

Partial result responses may repeat unresolved calls; parsing collapses only matching pending IDs/names/arguments, preserving existing results and leaving changed/completed calls distinct. Completed-prefix identity ignores historical call-ID normalization while retaining bound arguments/results.

Runtime dependency upgraded from inherited @bufbuild/protobuf 2.15.0 to 2.16.0; safe own-data argument maps preserve __proto__ and nested special keys through WKT tool schemas, native MCP delivery and serialized history. Original sourceDependency attribution remains unchanged.

Diagnostic serialization and file writes are best-effort with no stderr fallback; logger failures cannot skip lifecycle cleanup. Refresh failures discard their bodies and report HTTP status only. HTTP2 requests carry the required User-Agent. Native reads reject Pi Bash tail-truncation notices instead of reporting them as complete files.

The payload transport resolves its host Pi AI compat peer at module evaluation, not the first request, so the host extension loader can apply aliases in a clean install without a local runtime peer. A real-loader regression and packed SDK chat/tool/account-switch fixture cover this boundary. The Cursor bridge statically imports that adapter so native-import fast paths cannot bypass host aliases on its later module loads.
Streaming failures use OpenAI SSE error envelopes, not an invalid finish_reason or assistant content; the real Pi host regression preserves bridge and Connect error messages.
Non-streaming native tools are rejected and cannot renew the useful-output watchdog; only visible progress renews that clock.
Unhandled execs and failed native result encodings report through best-effort opt-in debug logs, never stderr.
Non-success HTTP2 responses become status-only Connect errors for streaming and nonzero unary exits with no retained body; streamed 401/402/403/429 failures retain account-recovery semantics.

Effort resolution never double-appends: a model id already ending in the live effort (stale raw ids restored from older sessions) resolves as-is instead of addressing a nonexistent `-high-high` variant.

Unified model listing: slot catalogs resolve through a per-slot policy (carrier lists the family union, siblings list nothing), sibling discovery re-lists the carrier best-effort, discovery marks feed saved-id supersede, and setup returns a reregister handle for carrier sync. Requests still authenticate per slot.
